**Finding: deviation (Section 7.2, ¶p0027)**

Section 7.2 runs the MFN against us — we would have to extend Silverline terms no less favourable than the best terms we give any other technology supplier. It is entirely open-ended (no defined product, no term limit, no reasonable-comparison carve-outs), so it fails the fallback position and falls into walk-away territory. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment.

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 7.2 imposes the MFN on us rather than in our favour: we must extend Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms given to any other technology supplier. It is open-ended — no defined product or service, no time limit, and no reasonable-comparison carve-outs — so it fails the fallback (MFN confined to a defined product for 12 months with carve-outs) and sits in walk-away territory. It also contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. Preferred remedy is deletion of the Customer-side obligation; no Vendor-granted MFN exists elsewhere that would be affected.

input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Section 21 sits at the preferred position. The cap is expressly mutual and set at the greater of Fees "paid or payable" in the twelve months preceding the event and USD 1,000,000 (21.1); "Fees" (1.5) captures recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the base is meaningful rather than illusory. The consequential-damages exclusion is mutual and is improved for us by confirming data restoration, replacement services, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages (21.2). "Excluded Claims" sit outside both the cap and the exclusion and cover confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP (21.3), and Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is expressly not "damages" limited by the Section. Section 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities, and 21.4 preserves the independence of each cap and survival beyond failure of an exclusive remedy. Minor point noted only: "Fees" excludes a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form states otherwise, slightly narrowing the fee base, but the USD 1,000,000 floor mitigates this. No cap, mutuality or carve-out defect exists, so no redline is proposed.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

Section 21 sits at the preferred position. The cap is expressly mutual and set at the greater of Fees "paid or payable" in the twelve months preceding the event and USD 1,000,000 (21.1); "Fees" (1.5) captures recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the base is meaningful rather than illusory. The consequential-damages exclusion is mutual and is improved for us by confirming data restoration, replacement services, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages (21.2). **Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The indemnity architecture in § 20, read with § 21.3, satisfies (and in places exceeds) our preferred position:

- **§ 20.1 — Vendor IP indemnity:** full defend/indemnify/hold harmless for third-party claims alleging the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate IP, extending to Customer, its Affiliates and their directors, officers, employees and agents. Notably there are *no* customer-modification/combination/specification carve-outs, which is better than the fallback.
- **§ 20.2 — Conduct indemnities:** Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/death/tangible property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud.
- **§ 20.4 — Procedure:** standard and reciprocal (prompt notice qualified by material prejudice, cooperation at the indemnifier's expense, control of defence, settlement-consent protections).
- **§ 20.5 — Infringement remedies:** procure, modify/replace without materially reducing functionality, or terminate with a straight-line three-year refund of prepaid and implementation Fees; Vendor cannot terminate unaffected Services. This is cross-referenced by our termination right in § 9.3.
- **§ 20.3 — Customer's reverse indemnity is narrow:** limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised and Customer's own violation of law, with carve-outs where the claim arises from Vendor Technology, modification, combination or instructions.
- **§ 21.3 — Cap treatment:** indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims, so they sit outside the general liability cap rather than being squeezed under the fallback's 3× super-cap.

No walk-away features (no one-way Customer indemnity, no IP exclusion). Nothing to flag under INDEMN.

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The indemnity package meets our preferred position. Section 20.1 gives a full Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims covering Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel, with no customer-modification or combination carve-outs. Section 20.2 adds Vendor indemnities for breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud. Section 20.4 sets standard reciprocal procedure (prompt notice with a material-prejudice qualifier, cooperation at the indemnifier's expense, control of defence, settlement consent protections), and 20.5 provides the procure/modify-or-replace/terminate-and-refund remedies (cross-referenced by the termination right in 9.3). Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 stays narrow — unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised and Customer's own violation of law — with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and instructions. Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under 21.3, so they sit outside the general liability cap, which is better than the fallback's 3× super-cap. No redline needed.

Original paragraphs:
p0082: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
p0083: 20.2 Vendor shall also defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the Customer indemnified parties from third-party claims to the extent arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage caused by Vendor; unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.
p0084: 20.3 Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor from a third-party claim alleging that unmodified Customer material supplied by Customer and used by Vendor strictly as authorized infringes an intellectual property right, or arising from Customer's violation of Applicable Law in its authorized use of the Services. Customer has no obligation to the extent a claim arises from Vendor Technology, modification, combination, or instructions.
p0085: 20.4 The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, and control of the defence, except delay excuses obligations only to the extent of material prejudice. The indemnifying Party may not settle a claim by admitting fault of, imposing non-monetary obligations on, or failing to fully release the indemnified Party without prior written consent.
p0086: 20.5 For an infringement claim, Vendor shall, at its expense and in addition to its defence obligations, procure continued use, modify or replace the affected item without materially reducing functionality, or, if neither is commercially reasonable, terminate the item and refund prepaid and implementation Fees on a straight-line three-year basis. Vendor may not terminate unaffected Services.
p0090: 21.3 “Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 21 sits at the preferred position. The cap is expressly mutual and set at the greater of Fees "paid or payable" in the twelve months preceding the event and USD 1,000,000 (21.1); "Fees" (1.5) captures recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the base is meaningful rather than illusory. The consequential-damages exclusion is mutual and is improved for us by confirming data restoration, replacement services, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages (21.2). "Excluded Claims" sit outside both the cap and the exclusion and cover confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP (21.3), and Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is expressly not "damages" limited by the Section. Section 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities, and 21.4 preserves the independence of each cap and survival beyond failure of an exclusive remedy. Minor point noted only: "Fees" excludes a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form states otherwise, slightly narrowing the fee base, but the USD 1,000,000 floor mitigates this. No cap, mutuality or carve-out defect exists, so no redline is proposed.

Original paragraphs:
p0088: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
p0089: 21.2 Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.
p0090: 21.3 “Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.
p0091: 21.4 The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

payload.heading: MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT
DEFINITIONS

“Affiliate” means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party. “Control” means ownership of more than fifty percent of the voting interests of an entity or the power to direct its management. An entity is an Affiliate only while that relationship continues.

“Applicable Law” means every statute, regulation, binding regulatory requirement, court order, and governmental rule applicable to a Party's performance under this Agreement, including laws concerning privacy, information security, export controls, employment, anti-bribery, and accessibility. Applicable Law does not include a private standard unless an Order Form expressly adopts it.

“Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.

“Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.

“Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.

“Order Form” means a written ordering document signed by authorized representatives of both Parties that references this Agreement and describes the Services, Deliverables, subscription quantities, service levels, Fees, and term purchased by Customer. A purchase order is an administrative convenience only and does not amend an Order Form or this Agreement.

“Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

“Vendor Technology” means Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation, routines, connectors, and other technology, and modifications of them that are not Deliverables and do not embody Customer Confidential Information. Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data or intellectual property owned by Customer before the Effective Date.
AGREEMENT STRUCTURE AND SCOPE

This Agreement establishes the legal terms under which Customer and its Affiliates may purchase Services from Vendor. No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.

Each Order Form is governed by this Agreement. If provisions conflict, the following order controls: a signed amendment that expressly identifies the provision amended; the applicable Order Form; any service-level exhibit; any security exhibit; and this Agreement. An Order Form prevails only for that Order Form and only when it expressly identifies the conflicting provision.

Vendor terms appearing on a website, click-through screen, invoice, quotation, acknowledgement, support portal, or purchase-order response do not apply, even if access to the Services technically requires acceptance. Customer's use of or payment for Services does not assent to additional or different terms.
SERVICES AND PERFORMANCE

Vendor shall provide the Services professionally, diligently, and in accordance with this Agreement, each Order Form, the documentation, agreed project plans, and Applicable Law. Vendor is responsible for the acts and omissions of its personnel, Affiliates, and subcontractors as though they were Vendor's own.
ORDER FORMS AND AFFILIATE ORDERS

An Order Form becomes binding when signed by both Parties. Changes in scope, assumptions, quantities, Fees, dependencies, or dates require a written change order signed by authorized representatives. Vendor shall not charge for work outside scope that Customer did not approve in a signed change order.
IMPLEMENTATION AND CHANGE CONTROL

Vendor shall prepare and maintain an implementation plan identifying tasks, owners, assumptions, dependencies, deliverables, acceptance criteria, risks, and target dates. The Parties will hold regular status meetings during implementation. Vendor shall keep accurate action and decision logs and furnish them to Customer on request.
ACCEPTANCE

Customer will have fifteen business days after delivery of a Deliverable to test it against the acceptance criteria in the applicable Order Form. Customer may accept it in writing or reject it by describing material nonconformities. Payment, productive use needed for testing, or silence does not constitute acceptance.

If Customer rejects a Deliverable, Vendor shall promptly correct the nonconformities at no additional charge and resubmit it for a new acceptance period. After two unsuccessful correction cycles, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and receive a refund of Fees paid for the rejected Deliverable and dependent Services Customer cannot reasonably use.
FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.
Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.

Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
TERM AND RENEWAL

This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.
Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.

On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.
TERMINATION

Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.

Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.

Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.

Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.
EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION

On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.

Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND DATA RETURN

Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.

Within thirty days after Customer's request, Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata reasonably necessary for use. Vendor shall not withhold Customer Data because of a fee dispute.

After Customer confirms successful return, Vendor shall securely delete remaining Customer Data from active systems and, as backups cycle, from backups, except for a copy required by Applicable Law. An authorized officer shall certify deletion in writing. Any retained copy remains protected and may not be used for another purpose.
CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES

Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE

Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.

For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.

Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.

Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.
INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES

As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.

Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.

Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.

No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.
CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY

Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data, use it for advertising, combine it with another customer's identifiable data, or train a generally available model on it without Customer's express written consent.

Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law concerning personal information. If Vendor processes personal information for Customer, the Parties' data-processing addendum is incorporated. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.
CONFIDENTIALITY

“Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.

The recipient shall use Confidential Information only to perform or exercise rights under this Agreement, protect it with at least reasonable care, and disclose it only to personnel, Affiliates, advisers, and subcontractors who need to know and are bound by confidentiality obligations. The recipient is responsible for their unauthorized use or disclosure.

On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.
INFORMATION SECURITY

Vendor shall maintain a written information-security program using administrative, technical, organizational, and physical safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of Customer Data and risk. At minimum, Vendor shall implement least-privilege access, multifactor authentication, encryption in transit and at rest, secure development, vulnerability management, logging, backup, business continuity, and annual workforce training.

Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay and no later than twenty-four hours after confirming unauthorized access to, acquisition, disclosure, alteration, loss, or destruction of Customer Data or a material compromise of systems used to provide the Services (a “Security Incident”). Notice will include known facts, affected data and systems, containment, and a contact.
INSURANCE

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.

Policies will be issued by reputable insurers and be primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary. On request, Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance and evidence of relevant coverage. Vendor shall give advance notice of cancellation or material reduction to the extent available from its insurer. Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.
WARRANTIES

Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.

For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.

Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.

For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.

Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.
INDEMNIFICATION

Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.

Vendor shall also defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the Customer indemnified parties from third-party claims to the extent arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage caused by Vendor; unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.

Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor from a third-party claim alleging that unmodified Customer material supplied by Customer and used by Vendor strictly as authorized infringes an intellectual property right, or arising from Customer's violation of Applicable Law in its authorized use of the Services. Customer has no obligation to the extent a claim arises from Vendor Technology, modification, combination, or instructions.

The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, and control of the defence, except delay excuses obligations only to the extent of material prejudice. The indemnifying Party may not settle a claim by admitting fault of, imposing non-monetary obligations on, or failing to fully release the indemnified Party without prior written consent.

For an infringement claim, Vendor shall, at its expense and in addition to its defence obligations, procure continued use, modify or replace the affected item without materially reducing functionality, or, if neither is commercially reasonable, terminate the item and refund prepaid and implementation Fees on a straight-line three-year basis. Vendor may not terminate unaffected Services.
LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.

Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.

“Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.

The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.
AUDIT RIGHTS
Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.

Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.

Audit findings are Customer Confidential Information and may be used only to enforce this Agreement. Vendor shall provide a copy of the final report. Payment of a shortfall resolves the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error.
RECORDS AND CUSTOMER ASSURANCE
ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL

Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.

Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.

For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.

Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.
PUBLICITY AND MARKS

Neither Party may issue a press release naming the other or use the other's names, trademarks, logos, or service marks in publicity, customer lists, case studies, or marketing without prior written consent in each instance. Customer may withdraw consent prospectively.
COMPLIANCE WITH LAW AND ETHICS

Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law in performing this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain policies reasonably designed to prevent bribery, corruption, forced labour, discrimination, retaliation, and conflicts of interest and shall provide annual compliance training to assigned personnel.

Vendor represents it has not offered and will not offer anything of value to improperly influence an official or private person in connection with this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain accurate books and promptly report a credible suspected violation materially related to the Services.

Each Party shall comply with applicable export-control and sanctions laws. Vendor is responsible for classifying Vendor Technology and identifying restrictions before delivery. Customer will not knowingly permit access from a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction contrary to written notice and Applicable Law.

Vendor shall comply with reasonable Customer workplace, safety, security, and acceptable-use policies supplied in advance while accessing Customer facilities or systems. A policy does not amend commercial terms or impose obligations unrelated to that access.
FORCE MAJEURE AND BUSINESS CONTINUITY

Neither Party is liable for delay caused by an event beyond its reasonable control that could not have been prevented through reasonable care, excluding inability to pay, staffing shortages, subcontractor failure that could reasonably be avoided, or a cyberattack preventable by required safeguards. The affected Party shall promptly notify the other and mitigate.

Vendor shall maintain and test at least annually business-continuity and disaster-recovery plans appropriate to the Services. Plans will address redundant systems, backups, recovery objectives, communications, and alternate personnel. Vendor shall provide a current executive summary on request.

If a force-majeure event materially prevents an affected Service for more than fifteen consecutive days, Customer may procure substitute services and suspend affected Fees. After thirty consecutive days, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without penalty and receive a refund of prepaid Fees for the unavailable period.
GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.

The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.

Before filing an ordinary commercial claim, a Party shall give notice and permit executives with settlement authority to meet in good faith within fifteen business days. This process does not delay urgent relief or a filing needed to preserve a limitations period. Discussions are compromise negotiations to the extent allowed by law.
NOTICES

Legal notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by nationally recognized overnight courier or certified mail, return receipt requested, to the address in the preamble and by email to the legal-notice address stated in the applicable Order Form. Operational notices may be delivered through agreed service channels.

Notice is effective on documented delivery, except a refusal is deemed delivery. A Party may change its notice address by notice under this Section. Email alone is insufficient for breach, termination, indemnity, assignment, or litigation notices unless receipt is affirmatively acknowledged.

This Agreement, its exhibits, and executed Order Forms are the entire agreement about their subject and supersede prior proposals, statements, and agreements. An amendment must be in a writing signed by authorized representatives of both Parties and expressly identify this Agreement.

Vendor remains responsible for output used in providing the Services.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.

Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.

Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.2","number":"14.2","heading":"Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.3","number":"14.3","heading":"Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.4","number":"14.4","heading":"No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15","number":"15","heading":"CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.1","number":"15.1","heading":"Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data, use it for advertising, combine it with another customer's identifiable data, or train a generally available model on it without Customer's express written consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.2","number":"15.2","heading":"Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law concerning personal information. If Vendor processes personal information for Customer, the Parties' data-processing addendum is incorporated. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16","number":"16","heading":"CONFIDENTIALITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.1","number":"16.1","heading":"“Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.2","number":"16.2","heading":"The recipient shall use Confidential Information only to perform or exercise rights under this Agreement, protect it with at least reasonable care, and disclose it only to personnel, Affiliates, advisers, and subcontractors who need to know and are bound by confidentiality obligations. The recipient is responsible for their unauthorized use or disclosure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.5","number":"16.5","heading":"On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17","number":"17","heading":"INFORMATION SECURITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.1","number":"17.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain a written information-security program using administrative, technical, organizational, and physical safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of Customer Data and risk. At minimum, Vendor shall implement least-privilege access, multifactor authentication, encryption in transit and at rest, secure development, vulnerability management, logging, backup, business continuity, and annual workforce training.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.2","number":"17.2","heading":"Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay and no later than twenty-four hours after confirming unauthorized access to, acquisition, disclosure, alteration, loss, or destruction of Customer Data or a material compromise of systems used to provide the Services (a “Security Incident”). Notice will include known facts, affected data and systems, containment, and a contact.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18","number":"18","heading":"INSURANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.1","number":"18.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.2","number":"18.2","heading":"Policies will be issued by reputable insurers and be primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary. On request, Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance and evidence of relevant coverage. Vendor shall give advance notice of cancellation or material reduction to the extent available from its insurer. Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19","number":"19","heading":"WARRANTIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.1","number":"19.1","heading":"Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.2","number":"19.2","heading":"For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.3","number":"19.3","heading":"Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.4","number":"19.4","heading":"For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.5","number":"19.5","heading":"Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20","number":"20","heading":"INDEMNIFICATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.1","number":"20.1","heading":"Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.2","number":"20.2","heading":"Vendor shall also defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the Customer indemnified parties from third-party claims to the extent arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage caused by Vendor; unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.3","number":"20.3","heading":"Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor from a third-party claim alleging that unmodified Customer material supplied by Customer and used by Vendor strictly as authorized infringes an intellectual property right, or arising from Customer's violation of Applicable Law in its authorized use of the Services. Customer has no obligation to the extent a claim arises from Vendor Technology, modification, combination, or instructions.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.4","number":"20.4","heading":"The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, and control of the defence, except delay excuses obligations only to the extent of material prejudice. The indemnifying Party may not settle a claim by admitting fault of, imposing non-monetary obligations on, or failing to fully release the indemnified Party without prior written consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.5","number":"20.5","heading":"For an infringement claim, Vendor shall, at its expense and in addition to its defence obligations, procure continued use, modify or replace the affected item without materially reducing functionality, or, if neither is commercially reasonable, terminate the item and refund prepaid and implementation Fees on a straight-line three-year basis. Vendor may not terminate unaffected Services.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21","number":"21","heading":"LIMITATION OF LIABILITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.1","number":"21.1","heading":"Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.2","number":"21.2","heading":"Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.3","number":"21.3","heading":"“Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.4","number":"21.4","heading":"The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22","number":"22","heading":"AUDIT RIGHTS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.1","number":"22.1","heading":"Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.2","number":"22.2","heading":"Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.3","number":"22.3","heading":"Audit findings are Customer Confidential Information and may be used only to enforce this Agreement. Vendor shall provide a copy of the final report. Payment of a shortfall resolves the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-23","number":"23","heading":"RECORDS AND CUSTOMER ASSURANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24","number":"24","heading":"ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.1","number":"24.1","heading":"Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.2","number":"24.2","heading":"Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.3","number":"24.3","heading":"For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.4","number":"24.4","heading":"Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-25","number":"25","heading":"PUBLICITY AND MARKS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-25.1","number":"25.1","heading":"Neither Party may issue a press release naming the other or use the other's names, trademarks, logos, or service marks in publicity, customer lists, case studies, or marketing without prior written consent in each instance. Customer may withdraw consent prospectively.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26","number":"26","heading":"COMPLIANCE WITH LAW AND ETHICS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.1","number":"26.1","heading":"Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law in performing this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain accurate books and promptly report a credible suspected violation materially related to the Services.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.3","number":"26.3","heading":"Each Party shall comply with applicable export-control and sanctions laws. Vendor is responsible for classifying Vendor Technology and identifying restrictions before delivery. A waiver must be written and signed by an authorized representative and applies only to the stated instance. Headings aid reference only. “Including” means “including without limitation,” and “or” is inclusive.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-30.4","number":"30.4","heading":"This Agreement, its exhibits, and executed Order Forms are the entire agreement about their subject and supersede prior proposals, statements, and agreements. An amendment must be in a writing signed by authorized representatives of both Parties and expressly identify this Agreement.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-30.5","number":"30.5","heading":"No person other than a Party, a Customer Affiliate ordering Services, a permitted successor, or an indemnified party has a right to enforce this Agreement. The Parties may amend or terminate it without another person's consent, subject to vested indemnity rights.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-30.6","number":"30.6","heading":"This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, each treated as an original, and by electronic signature. An electronic copy is effective as an original. Each signatory represents that they are authorized to bind the named Party.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-30.7","number":"30.7","heading":"Vendor shall not use an artificial-intelligence system to make a legally binding decision for Customer or submit Customer Confidential Information to a third-party model unless an Order Form expressly authorizes that use and specifies safeguards.
