No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
input.rationale: The warranty package meets the preferred position. Section 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus material conformance to documentation and specifications; 19.2 gives a 90-day Deliverable conformance warranty (running from the later of delivery or acceptance) and a hosted-Services conformance warranty for the whole subscription term, which exceeds the 12-month software benchmark; 19.3 adds no-malicious-code and compliance-with-Applicable-Law warranties; and 19.4 supplies the full remedy ladder of prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, with termination and refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. The disclaimer in 19.5 is limited to implied warranties and expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranties. No redline needed.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding submitted: deviation (AUDIT).**

- **Problem:** § 22.1 (p0093) allows Vendor to "audit Customer at any time without notice" and to "remotely access Customer's systems and records" — unlimited, unannounced audits with remote system access, which is walk-away territory under the rule and fails even the fallback (once per year, 15 days' notice, no system access). Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 22.1 grants unlimited, unannounced audits of Customer plus remote access to our systems — squarely in walk-away territory and well short of the fallback (once per year on 15 days' notice, no system access). It also contradicts Section 22.2, which already bars Vendor and its auditor from accessing Customer systems directly. Cost allocation in 22.2 (Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds five percent) and confidentiality of findings in 22.3 already meet the preferred position, so the redline is confined to 22.1: once per twelve months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, and no system access.

Original paragraphs:
p0093: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
p0094: 22.2 Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.
p0095: 22.3 Audit findings are Customer Confidential Information and may be used only to enforce this Agreement. Vendor shall provide a copy of the final report. Payment of a shortfall resolves the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 2.1 expressly disclaims any minimum quantity or purchase commitment and confirms that declining to place further Order Forms is neither a breach nor a shortfall, so fees are payable only for Services actually ordered — the preferred position. Section 7.1 further bars any unidentified minimum-use or similar charge, and § 12.3 records that we have made no minimum-volume commitment. No take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or volume cap on our usage appears anywhere in the document, so no redline is needed.

p0050: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:

Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: Section 7.6 imposes liquidated damages running against us — USD 25,000 per day for "any delay in providing a dependency" — which is the wrong direction under this rule and has no cap or materiality threshold, so it is triggered by trivial breaches and can accumulate well beyond the fallback of a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees. content.text:
**Finding: deviation (Section 7.6, ¶p0032) — high severity.**

Section 7.6 requires *us* to pay USD 25,000 per day as liquidated damages for "any delay in providing a dependency." That is liquidated damages running against the Customer, with no cap, no materiality threshold, and no cure period — it fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable LDs) and the fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees), and a daily penalty for minor delay sits in walk-away territory.

Supporting checks:
- No other LD, penalty, or termination-fee provision appears in the document (searches for "liquidated damages", "termination fee", "penalt" returned only §7.6, the Vendor IP indemnity, and a Customer-favourable force-majeure termination right).
- The §21.1 mutual cap does not neutralise the exposure: liability can still reach the greater of twelve months' Fees or USD 1,000,000, and "Excluded Claims" (§21.3) confirms the cap is not a substitute for removing the penalty.

Redline validated (ok:true) and submitted: delete the Customer-payable LD and substitute an equitable extension of Vendor's affected performance dates as Vendor's sole and exclusive remedy for a dependency delay — reaching the preferred position, with a three-months'-fees single amount available as a fallback if Vendor insists on a monetary construct.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 7.6 imposes liquidated damages running against us — USD 25,000 per day for "any delay in providing a dependency" — which is the wrong direction under this rule and has no cap or materiality threshold, so it is triggered by trivial breaches and can accumulate well beyond the fallback of a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees. The Section 21.1 mutual cap does not cure it: the exposure can still reach twelve months' Fees or USD 1,000,000, and a daily penalty for minor delay is walk-away territory. No offsetting service-credit or Vendor-side LD construct changes the analysis. We therefore delete the Customer-payable LD and substitute an equitable extension of Vendor's performance dates as its sole remedy, reaching the preferred position; if Vendor insists on a monetary construct, we would consider only a single amount capped at three months' fees.

Original paragraphs:
p0032: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Redwood Commerce Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Silverline Systems Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Redwood Commerce Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Silverline Systems Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.

Rendered redline:
p0032: 7.6 Customer shall not be liable to Vendor for any liquidated damages or penalties. If Customer delays providing a dependency, Vendor's affected performance dates and obligations shall be extended equitably, and such extension shall be Vendor's sole and exclusive remedy for the delay.

Comment:
[Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, and a USD 25,000 per-day charge for any dependency delay is disproportionate to the harm. We have replaced it with an equitable extension of Vendor's affected performance dates as Vendor's sole remedy for such delay.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: The warranty package meets the preferred position. Section 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus material conformance to documentation and specifications; 19.2 gives a 90-day Deliverable conformance warranty (running from the later of delivery or acceptance) and a hosted-Services conformance warranty for the whole subscription term, which exceeds the 12-month software benchmark; 19.3 adds no-malicious-code and compliance-with-Applicable-Law warranties; and 19.4 supplies the full remedy ladder of prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, with termination and refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. The disclaimer in 19.5 is limited to implied warranties and expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranties. No redline needed.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The § 19 warranty package sits at (indeed slightly above) the playbook's preferred position:

- **§ 19.1** — Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, per industry standards, plus material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications.
- **§ 19.2** — 90 days for Deliverables measured from the *later* of delivery or acceptance (better than delivery-only), and hosted Services conform *throughout the subscription term*, which exceeds the 12-month software benchmark.
- **§ 19.3** — No malicious code and compliance with Applicable Law, plus no functionality diminishment and open-source protection.
- **§ 19.4** — Full remedy ladder: prompt re-performance/repair/replacement at no charge, then termination of the affected item and refund of Fees paid; expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.
- **§ 19.5** — Disclaimer is confined to implied warranties and expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranties.

No walk-away "AS IS" language appears anywhere in the document.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
input.rationale: The warranty package meets the preferred position. Section 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus material conformance to documentation and specifications; 19.2 gives a 90-day Deliverable conformance warranty (running from the later of delivery or acceptance) and a hosted-Services conformance warranty for the whole subscription term, which exceeds the 12-month software benchmark; 19.3 adds no-malicious-code and compliance-with-Applicable-Law warranties; and 19.4 supplies the full remedy ladder of prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, with termination and refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. The disclaimer in 19.5 is limited to implied warranties and expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranties. No redline needed.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The § 19 warranty package sits at (indeed slightly above) the playbook's preferred position:

- **§ 19.1** — Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, per industry standards, plus material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications.
- **§ 19.2** — 90 days for Deliverables measured from the *later* of delivery or acceptance (better than delivery-only), and hosted Services conform *throughout the subscription term*, which exceeds the 12-month software benchmark.
- **§ 19.3** — No malicious code and compliance with Applicable Law, plus no functionality diminishment and open-source protection.
- **§ 19.4** — Full remedy ladder: prompt re-performance/repair/replacement at no charge, then termination of the affected item and refund of Fees paid; expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.
- **§ 19.5** — Disclaimer is confined to implied warranties and expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranties.

No walk-away "AS IS" language appears anywhere in the document.

The redline reaches the preferred position by removing Customer-payable LDs and substituting an equitable extension of Vendor's performance dates as Vendor's sole remedy — a substantively favorable and workable replacement rather than a bare deletion that would leave the delay unaddressed.

input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
input.rationale: Compliant at the preferred position; no redline proposed. Duration: § 19.2 (p0077) states the Deliverable conformance period as "ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later" — the period is spelled out in words rather than numerals, which is why an automated ">= 90 days / months / years" pattern check did not fire. Substantively the period is 90 days measured from the later of delivery or acceptance, so it meets (and by the measuring date slightly exceeds) the preferred 90-day services/deliverables benchmark, and hosted Services must "conform throughout the subscription term", which exceeds the 12-month software benchmark. Substance: § 19.1 (p0076) gives the professional and workmanlike warranty by qualified personnel per industry standards plus material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation and agreed specifications; § 19.3 (p0078) gives no-malicious-code and compliance-with-Applicable-Law warranties; § 19.4 (p0079) gives the full remedy ladder of prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, then termination of the affected item and refund of Fees paid, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. Disclaimer: § 19.5 (p0080) is confined to implied warranties and expressly provides that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or stated remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranties and there is no "AS IS" walk-away risk. No material term fails the preferred or fallback position.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Compliant at the preferred position; no redline proposed. You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Compliant at the preferred position; no redline and no counterparty comment are proposed, so the paragraphs stand unchanged. Period: the quoted sentence from § 19.2 (p0077) fixes the Deliverable conformance period at ninety days — i.e. 90 days, equal to the preferred 90-day benchmark and above the 30-day fallback — and it runs from the later of delivery or acceptance, which is more favourable to us than a delivery-only trigger. Hosted Services must conform "throughout the subscription term", a duration longer than the preferred 12 months for software. The deterministic ">= 90 days or months/years" check fails only because the drafter wrote the number in words ("ninety days") instead of numerals or a month/year unit; that is a formatting artifact and does not change the measured duration, so it does not displace the substantive reading. Remaining material terms: § 19.1 (p0076) warrants professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel to industry standards plus material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation and agreed specifications; § 19.3 (p0078) warrants no malicious code and compliance with Applicable Law; § 19.4 (p0079) gives prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, then termination of the affected item and a refund of Fees paid, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. § 19.5 (p0080) disclaims only implied warranties and states that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or stated remedy, so the express warranty survives and there is no "AS IS" walk-away exposure. Every material term meets the preferred position.

Original paragraphs:
p0076: 19.1 Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.
p0077: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
p0078: 19.3 Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.
p0079: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.
p0080: 19.5 Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Redwood Commerce Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Silverline Systems Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Redwood Commerce Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Silverline Systems Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Applicable Law: 1.2 “Applicable Law” means every statute, regulation, binding regulatory requirement, court order, and governmental rule applicable to a Party's performance under this Agreement, including laws concerning privacy, information security, export controls, employment, anti-bribery, and accessibility. Applicable Law does not include a private standard unless an Order Form expressly adopts it.
Deliverable: 1.4 “Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.
Fees: 1.5 “Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.
Order Form: 1.6 “Order Form” means a written ordering document signed by authorized representatives of both Parties that references this Agreement and describes the Services, Deliverables, subscription quantities, service levels, Fees, and term purchased by Customer. A purchase order is an administrative convenience only and does not amend an Order Form or this Agreement.
Services: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

Rendered redline:
p0076: 19.1 Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.
p0077: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
p0078: 19.3 Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.
p0079: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.
p0080: 19.5 Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-56e30d01","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.","rationale":"The indemnity package meets our preferred position. Section 20.1 gives a full Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims covering Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel, with no customer-modification or combination carve-outs. Section 20.2 adds Vendor indemnities for breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud. Section 20.4 sets standard reciprocal procedure (prompt notice with a material-prejudice qualifier, cooperation at the indemnifier's expense, control of defence, settlement consent protections), and 20.5 provides the procure/modify-or-replace/terminate-and-refund remedies (cross-referenced by the termination right in 9.3). Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 stays narrow — unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised and Customer's own violation of law — with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and instructions. Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under 21.3, so they sit outside the general liability cap, which is better than the fallback's 3× super-cap. No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-64bf8153","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.","rationale":"The IP package meets our preferred position in full. Section 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and pre-existing/independently developed IP, with no transfer to Vendor beyond a limited processing right to deliver the Services; Section 15.1 reinforces this by barring sale, advertising use, data commingling and model training without our written consent. Section 14.2 vests ownership of each Deliverable in Customer on creation with an express present assignment plus personnel assignments and further-assurance cooperation. Section 14.3 lets Vendor retain only Vendor Technology while pulling in the Section 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence (including rights to modify, create derivative works and use contractors) for any Vendor Technology embedded in or needed to use a Deliverable, and requires disclosure of embedded Vendor IP and consent before adding restrictive third-party material. Section 14.4 expressly negates joint ownership absent a signed separate instrument and keeps feedback rights with us. Two minor points noted only, not deviations: \"Deliverable\" (1.4) is limited to work product an Order Form identifies as created specifically for Customer, so Order Forms should be drafted to capture all bespoke work product; and the Deliverable ownership is conditioned on payment of the applicable Fees, which is customary. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-85b7fb6d","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","rationale":"Section 21 sits at the preferred position. The cap is expressly mutual and set at the greater of Fees \"paid or payable\" in the twelve months preceding the event and USD 1,000,000 (21.1); \"Fees\" (1.5) captures recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the base is meaningful rather than illusory. The consequential-damages exclusion is mutual and is improved for us by confirming data restoration, replacement services, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages (21.2). \"Excluded Claims\" sit outside both the cap and the exclusion and cover confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP (21.3), and Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is expressly not \"damages\" limited by the Section. Section 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities, and 21.4 preserves the independence of each cap and survival beyond failure of an exclusive remedy. Minor point noted only: \"Fees\" excludes a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form states otherwise, slightly narrowing the fee base, but the USD 1,000,000 floor mitigates this. No cap, mutuality or carve-out defect exists, so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-5ea675fe","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. That is the walk-away position (full-term exclusivity with no service-level or delivery-failure termination right), so it fails the fallback. It also directly contradicts Section 2.1 (no minimum quantity or purchase commitment) and Section 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity commitment), so deletion is the smallest edit that both reaches the preferred position and resolves the internal conflict. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.","rationale":"Section 13 meets the preferred position in full. 13.1 grants the subscription licence directly to Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf (with Authorized User sublicensing), so no notice mechanic is needed to add affiliates. 13.2 grants a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to Customer and its Affiliates for paid-up software and Vendor Technology embedded in Deliverables, with contractor support rights (confirmed by 14.3 for Vendor Technology needed to use a Deliverable). 13.3 permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24 (which allows assignment to an M&A successor without consent) and limits revocation or suspension to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure. The word \"revocable\" and any at-will revocation right are absent, and the 13.4 restrictions are standard and expressly preserve lawful reverse-engineering, authorized security testing, and use of Customer Data and output. It is open-ended — no defined product or service, no time limit, and no reasonable-comparison carve-outs — so it fails the fallback (MFN confined to a defined product for 12 months with carve-outs) and sits in walk-away territory. It also contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. Preferred remedy is deletion of the Customer-side obligation; no Vendor-granted MFN exists elsewhere that would be affected.","proposal":"Delete Customer-side MFN obligation in Section 7.2.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-4208d9d1","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","rationale":"The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use restriction binding us, which meets the preferred position. Section 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to develop, acquire, buy, build, sell, engage other suppliers, and operate in any field or territory, and records that we have given no non-compete commitment — language that benefits us and should be retained. Section 2.2's sole-and-exclusive-provider commitment is an exclusivity/minimum-source term addressed under the EXCLUSIVITY rule (and is in any event contradicted by Section 12.3), so we do not flag the same commercial term twice here. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-81304192","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.","rationale":"Order Forms auto-renew for twelve months (acceptable term length) but require one hundred eighty days' advance non-renewal notice. No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-9508e255","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 2.1 This Agreement establishes the legal terms under which Customer and its Affiliates may purchase Services from Vendor. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook. The core ri[REDACTED] provisions are strong and require no redline: Vendor's IP and operational indemnities (§ 20), ownership of Customer Data and Deliverables (§ 14, with the § 13.2 perpetual licence), the mutual liability cap with meaningful Excluded Claims (§ 21), our unrestricted assignment and change-of-control protections (§ 24), the subscription and paid-up licence grants (§ 13), New York law and venue (§ 28), the absence of minimum commitments (§ 2.1), post-termination transition and data return (§ 11), and Vendor insurance (§ 18).

Seven items require negotiation. Six are one-sided obligations running against us or gaps in our exit rights, and each fails the applicable fallback on a material term: exclusivity for the full term (§ 2.2), a Customer-payable daily liquidated damages penalty (§ 7.6), a Customer-side most-favoured-nation obligation (§ 7.2), a 180-day non-renewal notice window (§ 8.2), the absence of any termination-for-convenience right against a three-year auto-renewing term (§ 9), unlimited unannounced Vendor audits with remote system access (§ 22.1), and a one-way 18-month non-solicit/no-hire (§ 12.4). Notably, §§ 2.1 and 12.3 already record that we have made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment, so several of these clauses conflict with the Agreement's own terms and deletion is the cleanest fix.

One item — the performance warranty (§ 19) — is marked **needs review**: the substantive analysis reads as compliant at the preferred position, but automated verification did not pass, so we are not stating a conclusion until the warranty period and remedy language are confirmed by manual read.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 (with §§ 20.2–20.5, 21.3) | Full Vendor IP defence/indemnity; indemnities are Excluded Claims, so uncapped — better than fallback. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 (with §§ 13.2, 14.2–14.4, 15.1) | Customer owns data and Deliverables; perpetual paid-up licence to embedded Vendor Technology. Draft Order Forms to capture all bespoke work product (§ 1.4). |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.4, 18.2) | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; robust Excluded Claims. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Free Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors; Vendor restricted; no change-of-control termination or repricing. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 | Full-term sole-and-exclusive provider commitment, no category limit, no performance exit — walk-away; conflicts with §§ 2.1 and 12.3. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.6 | USD 25,000/day for "any delay in providing a dependency"; no cap, no materiality threshold — walk-away. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2–13.4) | Licence extends to Affiliates and contractors; no at-will revocation. |
| High | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 | Open-ended MFN running against us; no product, time or comparison limits — walk-away; conflicts with § 12.3. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction; § 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to operate — retain. |
| High | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | § 8.2 | 180-day non-renewal notice is double the 90-day walk-away threshold; pricing limb (§ 8.3, lesser of CPI/3%) is compliant. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 9 | No Customer convenience right against a three-year term with 12-month auto-renewals (§ 8.1–8.2) — walk-away. Vendor has none either. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 22.1 | Unlimited, unannounced audits plus remote access to our systems — walk-away; contradicts § 22.2. Cost (§ 22.2) and confidentiality (§ 22.3) are compliant. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 (with §§ 28.2–28.3) | New York law and exclusive New York County venue; no arbitration provision. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2.1 (with §§ 7.1, 12.3) | No minimum quantity, take-or-pay or shortfall penalty. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | One-way 18-month no-solicit/no-engage covering any Vendor employee, no carve-outs; no-hire element edges into walk-away; conflicts with § 12.3. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 (with §§ 11.2–11.3, 10.1–10.2) | Six months' assistance at expiring Order Form rates; data return in 30 days; deletion only after confirmed return. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Needs review** | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.2–19.5) | Substantive read is compliant at the preferred position (90-day Deliverable period from later of delivery or acceptance; Services conform throughout the term), but verification did not pass. Confirm manually before we close this item. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) | CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, EL 1M for term plus one year; insurance does not cap liability. |

---

## Walk-away items

The following clauses sit in walk-away territory or fail the fallback on a material term and cannot be accepted as drafted:

1. **§ 2.2 — Exclusivity.** Full-term exclusivity for the whole hosted analytics services line, with no category narrowing, no 12-month limit and no service-level or delivery-failure exit. We propose deletion; if exclusivity is commercially necessary, the fallback is a defined category, 12 months, and automatic termination on missed service levels.
2. **§ 7.6 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** USD 25,000 per day for any dependency delay, uncapped and with no materiality threshold; the § 21.1 mutual cap does not cure exposure that can still reach 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000. We propose deleting the LD and substituting an equitable extension of Vendor's performance dates as its sole remedy; at most we would consider a single amount capped at three months' fees.
3. **§ 7.2 — Customer-side MFN.** Open-ended obligation to extend Vendor our best supplier terms, with no defined product, time limit or comparison carve-outs. We propose deletion, consistent with § 12.3.
4. **§ 8.2 — 180-day non-renewal notice.** Double the 90-day walk-away threshold and well beyond the 60-day fallback maximum. We propose 30 days plus a Vendor renewal reminder 60 days before renewal; 60 days is available as a fallback.
5. **§ 9 — No termination for convenience.** No general Customer exit against a three-year term with automatic 12-month renewals. We propose a new § 9.4: 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no early-termination fee, and confirmation that Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right; 60 days is available as a fallback.
6. **§ 22.1 — Vendor audit rights.** Audits at any time without notice, plus remote access to our systems. We propose limiting to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, and no system access — which also aligns § 22.1 with § 22.2.
7. **§ 12.4 — One-way non-solicit/no-hire.** 18 months post-termination, covering any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term, extending to "engage", with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. We propose deletion, consistent with § 12.3; a narrow mutual version is available as a fallback.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven negotiation items above, with playbook comments stating our position and the offered fallback for each. Deletions (§§ 2.2, 7.2, 12.4) should be framed by reference to §§ 2.1 and 12.3, which already record that we made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment — these are internal-consistency fixes as much as commercial asks.
2. **Confirm the four non-negotiable positions** in the cover note: deletion of the Customer-payable daily LD (§ 7.6), removal of unannounced audits and remote system access (§ 22.1), a Customer termination-for-convenience right (new § 9.4), and a non-renewal window no longer than 60 days (§ 8.2).
3. **Complete the warranty review.** Manually confirm the § 19.2 Deliverable conformance period and trigger and the § 19.4 remedy language before we close the WARRANTY item; verification did not pass, so we are not recording a conclusion yet. No redline or counterparty comment is proposed pending that check.
4. **Business input on exclusivity (§ 2.2).** Confirm whether any exclusivity is commercially required; if not, we press for straight deletion.
5. **Order Form drafting note to the deal team.** "Deliverable" (§ 1.4) captures only work product an Order Form identifies as created specifically for Customer, so each Order Form must expressly identify all bespoke work product to secure our § 14.2 ownership.
6. **Retain the favourable provisions** on any counterparty turn: §§ 12.3, 20.1–20.5, 21.1–21.4, 24.1–24.4, 13.1–13.3, 11.1–11.3 and 18.1–18.2 should not be reopened or diluted."}
